text:
He turns the wheel of the Dharma of discipline.
It is fitting that he hold the wheel.
His speech is good, pleasing,
and always free from childish beings.
It is pleasing, good, and pleasant to the ear,
and it is agreeable and delightful.
It satisfies the mind and gives great happiness.
The Buddha speaks what is called “gentle.”
By the special qualities of the Tathāgata,
his power is not to be known.
His sons who have entered the grounds
are as numerous as the past buddhas.
You, Lord of the Gods, are special in the world,
but you cannot know the good Sage.
The gods of the form and formless realms, the gods of the desire realm,
and humans are born from mind.
In the world of the accomplished yogis,
all the special ones are like that, and so are the best of humans.
Those who know your greatness
are not sentient beings.
Those who know your greatness
are the buddhas who are called “Gentle.”
The one who is called “Gentle Splendor”
is named by the buddhas of the past.
The one who is named in this way
is the one who is called “Gentle Splendor.”
The buddhas of the past, future, and present
are the ones who are called “Gentle Splendor.”
With a pure mind, undistracted and one-pointed,
you hear your name in the midst of the assembly.
By this, may they attain knowledge and peace.
May they attain the supreme enlightenment that ends existence.
May all mantras be accomplished.
May all beings be born in the higher realms.

As soon as the Blessed One Śākyamuni entered into meditative equipoise,
blue, yellow, white, crimson, and crystal-colored light rays emerged from the curl of hair between his eyebrows.
They illuminated this entire buddha realm,
and also illuminated other world systems.
All the planets and stars were instantly outshone and drawn in.
Having drawn them in, he properly assigned them to their respective places.
By the blessing of the Buddha, they were summoned to the mandala of the retinue and disappeared into the tuft of hair between the Buddha's eyebrows.
All the planets, stars, and constellations lost their light and became distressed and terrified. They took refuge in the Blessed One Śākyamuni and joined their palms in supplication.
Thus they fell to the ground again and again.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni spoke to all the planets, stars, and constellations,
in order to guide those who are wise and those who are childish and ignorant.
"O friends, gods and men, listen!
" "The world is based on the actions of beings.
" "The body of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is also accomplished by it.
" "The world with its gods and asuras is also based on it.
"
